passages.passageHtml:
To answer Questions 312 through 316, use the following excerpt from Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.'s famous "I Have a Dream" speech, which he delivered during the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom on August 28, 1963.

As we walk, we must make the pledge that we shall always march ahead. We cannot turn back. There are those who are asking the devotees of civil rights, "When will you be satisfied?" We can never be satisfied as long as the Negro is the victim of the unspeakable horrors of police brutality. We can never be satisfied, as long as our bodies, heavy with the fatigue of travel, cannot gain lodging in the motels of the highways and the hotels of the cities. We cannot be satisfied as long as the Negro's basic mobility is from a smaller ghetto to a larger one. We can never be satisfied as long as our children are stripped of their selfhood and robbed of their dignity by signs stating "For Whites Only." We cannot be satisfied as long as a Negro in Mississippi cannot vote and a Negro in New York believes he has nothing for which to vote. No, no, we are not satisfied, and we will not be satisfied until justice rolls down like waters and righteousness like a mighty stream...

I say to you today, my friends, so even though we face the difficulties of today and tomorrow, I still have a dream. It is a dream deeply rooted in the American dream. I have a dream that one day this nation will rise up and live out the true meaning of its creed: "We hold these truths to be self-evident: that all men are created equal."

Use the following information for Questions 318 through 321.

When America entered the war in 1917, Congress passed a law called the Espionage Act, which said that during wartime it was illegal to obstruct the draft (forcing civilians to join the armed forces). Charles Schenck was against the war, so he mailed thousands of pamphlets to men who had been drafted, telling them that the government had no right to send American citizens to other countries to kill people. The government accused Schenck of violating the Espionage Act and brought Schenck to trial. The case was decided by the Supreme Court, in 1919, in favor of the United States.

Justice Holmes admitted that "in many places and in ordinary times," Schenck would have had a right to say everything that he said in his pamphlets. However, Holmes said, how far a person's freedom of speech extends depends on the circumstances. "The question in every case," he said, "is whether the words are used in such circumstances and are of such a nature as to create a clear and present danger that they will bring about the substantive evils that Congress has a right to prevent.... The most stringent protection of free speech would not protect a man in falsely shouting fire in a theatre and causing a panic."

Use the following information for Questions 325 through 329.

The Electoral College system consists of 538 electors. A majority, or 270 electoral votes, is required to elect the president. Each state is allotted one elector for each of its members in the House of Representatives (which is based on the state's population) plus two additional electors to account for the state's two senators. The following figure shows the results of the 2016 presidential election. Senators are elected to six-year terms, and members of the House are elected to two-year terms.

Use the following information for Questions 330 through 334.

Over the years, several changes or amendments have been made to the U.S. Constitution. There have been a total of 27 amendments. The first ten amendments are collectively known as the Bill of Rights. This table summarizes a few of these amendments.

AmendmentDateSummary
First1791Freedom of speech, religion, press, assembly, and petition
Second1791Right to bear arms
Fifth1791Right to avoid self-incrimination, right to trial, due process
Tenth1791Rights that are reserved to the states (issues that are not the responsibility of the federal government)
Eighteenth1919Prohibition
Nineteenth1920Women's right to vote
Twenty-first1933Repeal of the Eighteenth Amendment
Twenty-second1951Two-term limit on the president

Use the following information for Questions 335 through 338.

The following figure shows the percentage of the gross domestic product (GDP) that each country spends on healthcare and social care each year.

Laissez-faire capitalism is defined as the separation of the state and the economy. This economic policy leaves individuals and businesses alone and allows economic events to occur without interference from the government. Most Libertarians and some Republicans believe that laissez-faire capitalism is the best economic policy for the U.S. to follow.

Fossil fuels, such as coal and natural gas, consist of hydrocarbons that are derived from the remains of organisms. Many countries obtain most of their energy needs by burning fossil fuels. The combustion of fossil fuels produces heat, carbon dioxide, and water. Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming when present in excess in the atmosphere.

Use the following information for Questions 341 through 343.

On October 29, 1929, the New York Stock Exchange suffered its worst day ever, wiping out billions of dollars of investors' money in a single day that became known as Black Tuesday. America and the rest of the world spiraled into their longest and deepest economic downturn, which lasted until 1939.

In the 1930s, President Roosevelt issued a series of reforms intended to improve the economy.

questions.questionHtml: What problem was Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. trying to highlight?

options.A: the problem of sexual harassment for females in the United States
options.B: the problem of racial inequality for African Americans in the United States
options.C: the problem of income inequality for the very poor compared to the top 1 percent
options.D: the problem of having unrealistic dreams and how to eliminate them

questions.explanationHtml: Dr. King described the racial inequality that African Americans in the United States faced on a daily basis, so Choice (B) is correct. You can eliminate Choices (A) and (C) because there's no mention of sexual harassment or income inequality. You can also reject Choice (D) — the speech is called "I Have a Dream," not "I Don't Want to Have a Dream."

questions.questionHtml: According to Dr. King's speech in 1963, African Americans were discriminated against in each of the following ways EXCEPT

options.A: they were often victims of police brutality.
options.B: they were not allowed to stay in 'White Only' hotels.
options.C: they could not get good reception for their mobile phones in the large ghettos.
options.D: they were still denied the right to vote in some parts of the country.

questions.explanationHtml:
When Dr. King said that "the Negro's basic mobility is from a smaller ghetto to a larger one," he wasn't referring to mobile phones (which weren't available until many decades later). He was instead referring to how difficult it was for people born in the ghetto to ever escape them; therefore, Choice (C) is the correct answer.

Dr. King mentioned that African Americans in the United States were often victims of police brutality, so you can eliminate Choice (A). Choice (B) is incorrect because many hotels did ban African Americans from staying there during the 1960s. Choice (D) is also incorrect because the speech mentions that African Americans were still being prevented from voting in Mississippi.

questions.questionHtml: Toward the end of his speech, Dr. King used the quote "We hold these truths to be self-evident: that all men are created equal," taken from the Declaration of Independence. Why did Dr. King include this quote in his speech?

options.A: He was pointing out the differences between the rights of men and the rights of women.
options.B: He was trying to convince the audience that African Americans are superior to white Americans and should be treated as such.
options.C: He wanted African Americans to declare their independence from the United States.
options.D: He wanted to point out the hypocrisy of people who agree with the Declaration of Independence but don't agree with equal rights for African Americans.

questions.explanationHtml: Dr. King wanted to point out the hypocrisy of people who claim to believe that "all men are created equal" but don't agree with equal rights for African Americans, making Choice (D) the correct answer. You can reject Choices (A), (B), and (C) because they are not supported by the speech.

questions.questionHtml: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. also led many protests for civil rights during this period of history. What does the term "civil rights" mean in this context?

options.A: the rights and freedoms that every citizen has always enjoyed equally
options.B: the rights and freedoms that only African Americans have always benefited from
options.C: the rights and freedoms that ensure every citizen's ability to participate equally in social and political life
options.D: the rights and freedoms required by state law but not federal law

questions.explanationHtml: Civil rights refers to the rights and freedoms that ensure every citizen's ability to participate equally in social and political life, making Choice (C) correct. If Choice (A) were true, there would be no need for the civil rights movement, because everyone would already be enjoying their rights. Choice (B) can be eliminated for the same reason. Civil rights are protected by federal law, so you can reject Choice (D).

questions.questionHtml: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was eventually successful in helping to bring an end to racial segregation in the United States. Which of the following best describes racial segregation?

options.A: the separation of different races in public institutions and daily life
options.B: a belief that the United States Constitution should apply only to "the right kind of people"
options.C: the system that helps include more minorities in everyday events
options.D: a scientific theory that supports the ideas and beliefs of white supremacists

questions.explanationHtml: Racial segregation describes the separation of different races in public institutions and daily life, so Choice (A) is correct. You can reject Choice (B) because although it describes a racist point of view, it doesn't describe racial segregation. Choices (C) and (D) are incorrect and can therefore be rejected.

questions.questionHtml: Every decade, the United States Census Bureau takes a census of the population. Which of the following best describes the U.S. Census?

options.A: calculations based on global warming
options.B: an unconstitutional practice that should be stopped immediately
options.C: demographic information (such as age, ethnicity, and level of education) taken every ten years
options.D: a tax that every citizen needs to pay every ten years

questions.explanationHtml: Every decade, the United States Census Bureau takes citizens' demographic information (such as age, ethnicity, and level of education) in order to track how the population is changing. Therefore, Choice (C) is correct. You can reject Choices (A) and (D) because the census has nothing to do with global warming and is not a tax.

questions.questionHtml: Which important amendment did the case refer to?

options.A: First Amendment
options.B: Second Amendment
options.C: Eighteenth Amendment
options.D: Nineteenth Amendment

questions.explanationHtml: The First Amendment protects freedom of speech, so Choice (A) is the best answer. The Second Amendment protects the right to bear arms, so you can reject Choice (B). The Eighteenth Amendment banned the sale of alcohol, and the Nineteenth Amendment refers to women's suffrage, so Choices (C) and (D) are wrong.

questions.questionHtml: Under which special circumstances did the Supreme Court state that limits to freedom of speech would apply?

options.A: when an individual says something that the president disagrees with
options.B: when an individual says something that the Supreme Court disagrees with
options.C: when the United States is at war and an individual's speech may cause a clear and present danger to national security
options.D: when the United States presents a clear and present danger to an individual

questions.explanationHtml: According to the passage, Justice Holmes stated that the question in every case "is whether the words are used in such circumstances and are of such a nature as to create a clear and present danger," so Choice (C) is correct.

questions.questionHtml: Based upon the outcome of this Supreme Court decision, would you have the right to falsely shout, "Fire!" in a crowded cinema?

options.A: Yes, because freedom of speech is protected by the First Amendment.
options.B: Yes, because freedom of speech is protected by the Second Amendment.
options.C: No, because the First Amendment doesn't protect false speech that can cause panic.
options.D: No, because the Second Amendment doesn't protect false speech that can cause panic.

questions.explanationHtml: The passage says Justice Holmes stated that the First Amendment "would not protect a man in falsely shouting fire in a theatre and causing a panic," so the correct answer is Choice (C). Choices (B) and (D) can be rejected because they refer to the Second Amendment (rather than the First Amendment).

questions.questionHtml: Which war did the United States enter in 1917?

options.A: World War I
options.B: World War II
options.C: U.S. Civil War
options.D: Cold War

questions.explanationHtml: World War I started in 1914 and ended in 1918. The United States entered World War I in 1917, making Choice (A) the correct answer. You can reject the other answers because World War II lasted from 1939 to 1945, the U.S. Civil War was from 1861 to 1865, and the Cold War started in 1945.

questions.questionHtml: What was the name of the period from 1917 until 1933 during which the sale or consumption of alcohol was illegal in the United States?

options.A: the Great Depression
options.B: Prohibition
options.C: the Cold War
options.D: the Dust Bowl

questions.explanationHtml: The Eighteenth Amendment (Prohibition) was passed in 1917 and prohibited the sale or consumption of alcohol in the United States. It was repealed in 1933 via the Twenty-first Amendment. Hence, Choice (B) is the correct answer.

questions.questionHtml: The graph suggests that which of the following statements is true?

options.A: More Native Americans died during the second half of the century than during the first half of the century.
options.B: Most Native Americans immigrated to other countries during the 16th century.
options.C: Approximately 20 million Native Americans died during the first half of the century.
options.D: The Native American population remained stable throughout the 16th century.

questions.explanationHtml: From the graph, you can see that the population of Native Americans dropped sharply during the first half of the 16th century, making Choice (A) false and Choice (C) true. The population of Native Americans did not fall due to emigration or suicide, so you can reject Choices (B) and (D).

questions.questionHtml: What caused the sharp decline in the Native-American population during the 16th century?

options.A: Native Americans were executed by the Spanish conquistadors.
options.B: Most of the Native Americans emigrated to escape from the Spanish invaders.
options.C: Native Americans were killed off by diseases brought by the European invaders.
options.D: The suicide rate among Native Americans rose sharply during the 16th century.

questions.explanationHtml: Although the Spanish conquistadors did kill some of the Native Americans, most of them were killed off by the new diseases that the Europeans brought to the New World. Choice (C) is the correct answer.

questions.questionHtml: Which candidate did most Americans vote for?

options.A: Donald Trump
options.B: Hillary Clinton
options.C: Jill Stein
options.D: Gary Johnson

questions.explanationHtml: You can see from the figure that Hillary Clinton received over 62.5 million votes, which is more than the 61 million votes that Donald Trump received, so the correct answer is Choice (B).

questions.questionHtml: How many Electoral College votes does a candidate need to become president?
questions.explanationHtml: The passage tells you that a candidate needs at least 270 electoral votes to become president, so the correct answer is Choice (B).

questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements is FALSE?

options.A: The United States is both a republic and a democracy.
options.B: The outcome of the Electoral College system is always in agreement with the outcome of the popular vote.
options.C: Each state has two senators.
options.D: The number of electors that each state has is based primarily on the state's population.

questions.explanationHtml: You can see from the figure that the outcome of the Electoral College system is not always in agreement with the outcome of the popular vote. In 2016, Donald Trump won the Electoral College vote (304 to 232), whereas Hillary Clinton won the popular vote; Choice (B) is a false statement and is therefore the correct answer. A common definition of republic is "a political order in which the supreme power lies in a body of citizens who are entitled to vote for officers and representatives responsible to them." A common definition of democracy is "government by the people, exercised either directly or through elected representatives" — hence, the United States is both a republic and a democracy, making Choice (A) a true statement.

questions.questionHtml: Based on the information in the passage, which of the following is a true statement?

options.A: The number of members that a state has in the U.S. Senate is based on the state's population, whereas each state always has two members in the U.S. House of Representatives.
options.B: The number of members that a state has in the U.S. House of Representatives is based on the state's population, whereas each state always has two members in the U.S. Senate.
options.C: The number of members that a state has in both the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate is based on the state's population.
options.D: Each state always has two members in both the U.S. Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives.

questions.explanationHtml: The information in the passage tells you that the number of members that a state has in the U.S. House of Representatives is based on the state's population, whereas each state always has two members in the U.S. Senate, making Choice (B) the correct answer.

questions.questionHtml: When a senator is elected, how long is his or her term in office?

options.A: 2 years
options.B: 8 years
options.C: 4 years
options.D: 6 years

questions.explanationHtml: You are told in the passage that senators are elected to six-year terms. Hence, Choice (D) is correct.

questions.questionHtml: Which amendment prohibits the President of the United States from running for a third term during an election?

options.A: First Amendment
options.B: Second Amendment
options.C: Eighteenth Amendment
options.D: Twenty-second Amendment

questions.explanationHtml: From the table, you can see that the Twenty-second Amendment sets a two-term limit on the president (which means that no person can be president for more than two terms). If the President of the United States has already been president for two terms, he cannot run for a third term, so Choice (D) is the correct answer.

questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a true statement regarding the U.S. Constitution and its amendments?

options.A: The U.S. Constitution can never be changed.
options.B: Amendments are merely suggestions, so they aren't legally binding.
options.C: An amendment can never be changed once it becomes the law of the land.
options.D: An amendment can be changed later if necessary.

questions.explanationHtml: From the table, you can see that the Twenty-first Amendment repealed the Eighteenth Amendment regarding Prohibition, so Choice (D) is the correct answer. You can reject Choice (A) because amendments do change (amend) the Constitution. Once they're ratified, amendments are legally binding, so you can also eliminate Choice (B).

questions.questionHtml: The first ten amendments were collectively known as the Bill of Rights. What was the main purpose of the Bill of Rights?

options.A: to protect the federal government from the people by placing limits on their individual rights
options.B: to protect the people and the states from the federal government by guaranteeing their basic individual rights
options.C: to protect the president from the states by placing limits on state rights
options.D: to replace the original Constitution

questions.explanationHtml: From the table, you can see that the First, Second, and Fifth Amendments all refer to protecting the rights of the individual. The Tenth Amendment also protects the rights of the states by placing limits on the federal government; hence, Choice (B) is the correct answer. You can reject Choices (A) and (C) because they describe the opposite of what the Bill of Rights accomplished. Choice (D) is incorrect because the Bill of Rights amended the Constitution, it didn't replace it.

questions.questionHtml: The National Rifle Association (NRA) strongly supports which amendment?

options.A: First Amendment
options.B: Second Amendment
options.C: Fifth Amendment
options.D: Tenth Amendment

questions.explanationHtml: From the table, you can see that the Second Amendment protects the right to bear arms (gun ownership). The NRA opposes any law that attempts to limit the right to bear arms, so Choice (B) is the correct answer.

questions.questionHtml: Which amendment allows a defendant to remain silent when they are being questioned about an issue that might incriminate them?

options.A: First Amendment
options.B: Fifth Amendment
options.C: Eighteenth Amendment
options.D: Twenty-first Amendment

questions.explanationHtml: From the table, you can see that the Fifth Amendment gives you the right to avoid self-incrimination, the right to trial, and the right to due process, so Choice (B) is the correct answer.

questions.questionHtml: Which of the following best describes gross domestic product (GDP)?

options.A: the total value of all the repulsive or unattractive household products that each country makes
options.B: the total value of all the services provided and goods produced in a country in one year
options.C: the total value of all the tax revenue that a country collects in one year
options.D: the total value spent on health and social care by each country in one year

questions.explanationHtml: Choice (B) provides the definition of GDP and is therefore the correct answer. Choice (A) is amusing but obviously incorrect. Choices (C) and (D) are also false statements.

questions.questionHtml: Which country spends the highest percentage of its GDP on healthcare?

options.A: France (FRA)
options.B: the United Kingdom (UK)
options.C: the United States (US)
options.D: Canada (CAN)

questions.explanationHtml: You can see from the figure that the United States spends 16 percent of its GDP on healthcare services, which is higher than the healthcare spending of the other countries. Hence, Choice (C) is correct.

questions.questionHtml: Which country spends the smallest percentage of its GDP on social care?

options.A: France (FRA)
options.B: the United Kingdom (UK)
options.C: the United States (US)
options.D: New Zealand (NZ)

questions.explanationHtml: You can see from the figure that the United States spends only 9 percent of its GDP on social care services, which is lower than the social care spending of the other countries. Hence, Choice (C) is correct.

questions.questionHtml: Regarding the 11 countries listed, which of the following is a true statement?

options.A: The United States spends the median total dollar amount on social and health services.
options.B: Canada spends approximately the same amount on healthcare as it does on social care.
options.C: The United States spends more than 30 percent of its GDP on health and social care.
options.D: New Zealand (NZ) cares less about its people than France (FRA).

questions.explanationHtml: You can see from the figure that Canada spends approximately the same percentage on healthcare (10 percent of its GDP) as it does on social care, making Choice (B) the correct answer. Although Choice (A) may appear to be true at first glance, the U.S. spends the median percentage of GDP, not the actual dollar amount (which is not given). You can reject Choice (C) because the U.S. spends less than 30 percent of its GDP on its health and social care. Choice (D) is wrong because it represents an opinion rather than a fact — just because New Zealand spends a lower percentage of its GDP does not mean that it cares less for its people.

questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is an opinion rather than a fact about laissez-faire capitalism?

options.A: Most communist countries would disagree with the main idea of laissez-faire capitalism.
options.B: Most Libertarians believe in laissez-faire capitalism.
options.C: Laissez-faire capitalism is irresponsible and should be outlawed.
options.D: Laissez-faire capitalism means the government plays no major role in the economy.

questions.explanationHtml: Only Choice (C) represents an opinion rather than a factual statement, making it the correct answer. The passage tells you that laissez-faire capitalism means that the government plays no major role in the economy. Choices (A) and (D) are therefore factual statements and can be rejected. Choice (B) is also a factual statement.

questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a fact rather than an opinion about fossil fuels?

options.A: Fossil fuels should be banned because they are too dirty and expensive.
options.B: Many countries rely on fossil fuels as their major source of energy.
options.C: The United States should bury its fossil fuels so they don't contribute to global warming.
options.D: Fossil fuels are more economical than alternative sources of energy.

questions.explanationHtml: The question stem tells you that many countries obtain most of their energy needs by burning fossil fuels. Hence, Choice (B) is a factual statement, making it the correct answer. Each of the other answer choices is an opinion rather than a factual statement.

questions.questionHtml: What is the name of the period of economic decline that lasted from 1929 until 1939?

options.A: the Great Repression
options.B: the Great Recession
options.C: the Great Depression
options.D: the Great Downturn

questions.explanationHtml: The period of economic decline that lasted from 1929 until 1939 was known as the Great Depression, making Choice (C) the correct answer.

questions.questionHtml: What is the name of the series of reforms issued by President Roosevelt in the 1930s that were intended to improve the economy?

options.A: the New Deal
options.B: the Square Meal
options.C: the Raw Deal
options.D: Reconstruction

questions.explanationHtml: The New Deal was a series of reforms that President Franklin D. Roosevelt issued in the 1930s with the intent to improve the economy, making Choice (A) the correct answer. Choices (B) and (C) are common terms, but they don't refer to a series of reforms. Reconstruction, Choice (D), refers to the period of rebuilding that occurred shortly after the Civil War.

questions.questionHtml: What global event in 1939 helped the United States finally recover from its economic decline?

options.A: the start of World War I
options.B: the start of World War II
options.C: the end of World War II
options.D: the end of the Vietnam War

questions.explanationHtml: The start of World War II in 1939 helped the United States finally recover from the Great Depression, making Choice (B) the correct answer.
